title: Arithmetic Stein-degree bounds for log Calabi–Yau pairs
main_claim: For a projective lc Q-pair (X,B) of dimension d over any char-0 field k with H^0(O_X)=k and K_X+B ~Q 0, every prime component S of B with coefficient >= t has [k_S:k] <= N(d,t); hence Stein degree of S over k is bounded (contraction-to-a-point case of Birkar's Stein-degree conjecture).

issues.description: The argument needs the geometric n-complement to satisfy B^+ >= bS, so that D = n(B^+ - bS) is an effective member of |-nK-nbS|. This depends on Birkar 2019 Thm 1.7 being applied with coefficients in a hyperstandard set Phi(R) where 1-b lies in R. The paper says this but does not check it in detail.
issues.evidence: 'a finite rational set is contained in an appropriate hyperstandard set. We may replace n by a prescribed fixed multiple.' Birkar's Thm 1.7 gives B^+ >= B for coefficients in Phi(R), so this looks right.

issues.description: The construction of bounded resolutions in families over the field of definition (stratify the parameter space, resolve at generic points, spread out, use finite étale covers to count strata) is only sketched. It is standard, but the uniform bound M on the number of strata over arbitrary fields relies on this sketch.
issues.evidence: Proof paragraphs 2-4 of Lemma embedded: 'Stratify... spread... Noetherian induction'.

coverage:
Read the full paper (1179 lines) and checked every step of the main proof:
- Lemma constants: linear disjointness and the generic-fibre inequality.
- klt Q-factorial model, using the negativity lemma.
- Lemma positive-component: the scaling computation gives D_i.R<0, so S_i.R>0 and S is never contracted. In the Picard-number-one case, -K is ample and -K-bS is nef.
- Lemma complement: the general-member lc argument via the fixed part plus a base-point-free part, and descent using that k is infinite.
- Corollary finite-low: the log-discrepancy decomposition a(v,W,B_W)=a(v,W,H)+sum(1-b_i)v(H_i).
- Weighted-blowup uniqueness lemma.
- Main proof: places with log discrepancy below 1/n are lc places because a lies in Z/n. The extraction gives an epsilon-lc X_2, and epsilon-lc is preserved along the K-MMP.
- BAB orbit proposition: h^0 <= L^q+q; Pic is torsion-free via Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing; the Minkowski-type bound via reduction mod 3; determinant descent of L^r (x) det^-1. Rechecked the marked-degree bound by adjunction on a curve cut out by general members; the orbit size is at most [F:k]M!.
- Extraction of v_S with Gamma=(1-lambda)C_3; this model is Fano type over Z.
- Horizontal coefficient-one component: bigness of pi^*S_1 survives the pushforward.
- Lemma vertical: the MMP is an isomorphism over an open subset of Z; klt base point freeness; mP'=f^*T; T pulls back nontrivially to E^nu.
- Adjunction keeps the specified index n, and the different contains beta P|E.
- Tower of constant fields: [k_J:k]=[k_E:k][k_J:k_E].
- Incidence lemma: at most 2/b components through a codimension-two locus, via mult <= 2 on the smooth cover of a quotient singularity.
- Final recurrence: every recursive term is in strictly smaller dimension.

Not checked: the cited theorems themselves (Birkar 2019 and 2021, BCHM / Lyu–Murayama, BMT).
sibling_notes: Family 034 siblings (log abundance, uniform Iitaka, relative denominators) are a different strand and do not depend on this paper. This paper uses no companion papers, only published theorems: Birkar's bounded complements and BAB, BCHM via Lyu–Murayama, and BMT resolution. Its role is the arithmetic Stein-degree input (the 'SD' companion) cited by Uniform-Pluricanonical-Iitaka and Uniform-log-Iitaka. The main result here is unconditional given those standard theorems.
